title: 10-year housing and homelessness plan endorsed
subtitle: Lived expertise delegation, chronic homelessness progress update, public health school services, and funding for a lived expertise program
overview: The Community and Health Services Committee recommended that Council endorse the 2026–2036 Housing and Homelessness Plan {{vote:m2}}. The plan sets the Region's direction on housing and homelessness planning, investment, service coordination, monitoring and advocacy for the next decade. Staff said the province has already approved it, the previous plan has expired, and a deferral to the next term of Council would leave staff in limbo. Staff also said the plan is directional and does not commit funding. Resources and targets will depend on the budget process.

The committee heard from members of the Lived Expertise Engagement Program, who reviewed progress on 30 calls to action and said theirs is the only remaining local lived expertise advisory group. It also received, for information, the 2026 progress update on the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness and a report on Public Health school-based services. Staff reported that student immunization record compliance rose from about 85% to over 98%.
Under other business, staff agreed to send Council an overview of what the Region funds and where it could help sustain the lived expertise program. The next meeting is November 3, 2026.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council endorse the 2026–2036 Housing and Homelessness Plan as the Region's strategic direction for housing and homelessness work over the next decade {{vote:m2}}.

debate: Councillors asked why the plan came forward so close to the new term. Staff said it is a provincially legislated duty, the province has approved it, the old plan has expired, and deferral would leave staff unable to proceed with the new plan.

Several councillors asked about targets and funding. Staff said the plan is directional and commits no resources. Measurable targets depend on service levels set through the budget. One councillor asked for future reports to show the funding gaps behind actions marked as needing funding.

Councillors raised seniors, youth and disaggregated demographic data, including people with brain injury or addiction who need long-term supportive housing. Staff said a youth strategy is limited by staff capacity more than money, and said they would note interest in more detailed demographic data.

Staff said market rents rising out of reach of social assistance backs up the whole housing continuum. In answer to a question on OW and ODSP rates, staff said income was the top reason people gave for homelessness in the last count, so poverty must be addressed too.

Delegates described the loss of other lived expertise groups and asked for culturally responsive approaches and a homelessness advocacy office with one consistent support worker. Councillors supported these ideas, and one asked staff to look at co-funding the program.
